data.question_title: A body of mass 4 kg moving with velocity 12 m/s collides with another body of mass 6 kg at rest. If two bodies stick together after collision, then the loss of kinetic energy of system is
data.explanation_txt:
Given,

\(m_1 = 4kg \\ u_1 = 12m/s \\ m_2 = 6kg \\ u_2 = 0 m/s \)

Conservation of momentum yields,

\(m_1u_1 + m_2u_2 = (m_1+m_2)V \\ \Rightarrow 48 = 10 \times V \\ \Rightarrow V = 4.8 m/s\)

Loss in energy is:

\(\begin{align} \Delta KE &= \cfrac{1}{2} \left( (m_1+m_2)V^2 - m_1u_1^2 \right) \\ &= \cfrac{1}{2} (10 \times 4.8^2 - 4 \times 12^2) \\ &= 172.8 J \end{align} \)

data.question_title: Which source is associated with a line emission spectrum?
data.explanation_txt:
Neon light is produced when electron falls down from higher orbit to lower orbit in Neon atoms. This de-excitation of electrons produces light of specific frequency corresponding to the energy level difference between the orbits. Therefore, light emission in neon street light is emission line spectrum of Neon atom.

Electric fire and Sun produce light of all wavelength i.e. continuous spectrum as given by planck distribution.

Red traffic light is generally composed of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) and light is produced when electrons combine with holes which is also a continuous spectrum in a given range of wavelength. This can be explained from the following fact:

Semiconductor has a range of valence potential called valence band (energy level of non conducting electrons) and also a range of conduction potential called conduction band (energy level of conducting electrons). So, when an electron jumps from conduction band to valence band, light of wavelength with energy corresponding to that particular energy difference is produced. This energy difference is not same for all electrons combining with holes as conduction and valence state exists in a range.

data.question_title: The S.I. unit of radioactivity is
data.explanation_txt:
The Becquerel (Bq) is the SI derived unit of radioactivity. One becquerel is defined as the activity of a quantity of radioactive material in which one nucleus decays per second. The becquerel is therefore equivalent to an inverse second, s−1.

1 Rutherford = 106 disintegration per second i.e. 1060 Bq = 1 MBq

1 Curie = 3.7*1010 disintegration per second i.e 37*109 Bq = 37 GBq

Roentgen is a unit to measure exposure of \(X\)-rays and \(\gamma\)-rays.

data.explanation_txt:
Let

\[ x = 2 + \cfrac{1}{2 + \cfrac{1}{2 + \dots \, to \, \infty}} \]

Then we can write:

\[ x = 2 + \cfrac{1}{x} \]

On simplification,

\( x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0 \\ \Rightarrow x = \cfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4+4}}{2} \\ \Rightarrow x = 1 \pm \sqrt{2} \)

But as \(x > 0\), and \( \sqrt{2} > 1 \), \( 1- \sqrt{2} \) is discarded.

So, \(x = 1 + \sqrt{2} \)

data.question_title: A magnet is suspended in such a way that it oscillates in the horizontal plane. It makes 20 oscillations per minute at a place where dip angle is 30\(^\circ\) and 15 oscillations per min. at a place where dip angle is 60\(^\circ\). data.explanation_txt:
Let the total magnetic fields due to earth at two places be \(B_{1}\) and \(B_{2}\). If horizontal components be \(\left(B_{H}\right)_{1}\) and \(\left(B_{H}\right)_{2}\), respectively
then,
\(\begin{array}{l}{B_{H_{1}}=B_{1} \cos 30^{\circ} \text { and } B_{H_{2}}=B_{2} \cos 60^{\circ}} \\ {T_{1}=3 \sec \& \, T_{2}=4 \sec } \\ T = 2 \pi \sqrt{\cfrac{I}{MB_H}}\\ {\therefore \cfrac{B_{H_{1}}}{B_{H_{2}}}=\left(\cfrac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}\right)^{2} \Rightarrow \cfrac{B_{1} \cos 30^{\circ}}{B_{2} \cos 60^{\circ}}=\cfrac{16}{9}} \\ {\therefore \cfrac{B_{1}}{B_{2}}=16: 9 \sqrt{3}}\end{array}\)

data.question_title: 40ml of 0.1N HCl are mixed with 20ml of 0.1M \(\text{H\({}_{2}\)SO\({}_{4}\).}\) The strength of the resulting solution will be
data.explanation_txt:
20 ml of 0.1 M H\(_2\)SO\(_4\) = 20 ml of 0.2 N H\(_2\)SO\(_4\)

Strength of resulting solution \(=\cfrac{N_1V_1+N_2V_2}{V_1+V_2}=\cfrac{40 \times 0.1N + 20 \times 0.2N}{40+20}=\cfrac{8}{60}=0.133N\)

data.question_title: 100ml of 0.5N NaOH solution is added to 20ml of 1N HCl solution and 10ml of \(\text{3N-H\({}_{2}\)SO\({}_{4}\)}\) solution. The solution will be
data.explanation_txt:
100 ml of 0.5N NaOH = 50 ml of 1N base
20 ml of 1N HCl = 20 ml of 1N acid
10 ml of 3N \(H_{2}SO_{4}\) = 30 ml of 1N \(H_{2}SO_{4}\) = 30 ml of 1N acid

\(\therefore\) We can say 50 ml of 1N base reacts with 50 ml of acid to give neutral result.

data.question_title: When you sit in your local cinema hall enjoying the film that is being flashed on the screen in front of you, do you ever think of how films are made? Hundreds, perhaps thousands, of people may have spent a year or even longer working very hard to produce a film, which lasts a mere hour or two. Film making is nowadays a very big and complicated industry, involving large sums of money and occupying many hundreds of skilled technicians as well as actors and actresses. What happens when a film company decides to shoot a film? There must, of course, be a story. This may be based on a novel or a play, or it may be specially written for the film. From the story, whatever it is, a shooting script has to be prepared, which shows all the scenes, the ordering which they are to be photographed or shot the way the actors are to speak and moves, the position of the cameras for each scene, and so on. Then the producer and a director are appointed. The producer engages the actors and actresses, decides which scenes are to be taken in the studio and which outside or on ‘location’, and makes all the preliminary preparations. The director is the man who tells the actors what to do, and shows them how to act each scene. It is his job to interpret the script and translate the author’s words and instructions into a series of living scenes.
